greenhouse:Polderbyte:pb-1: Which of my projects should I mention for this role, and why?

Lead with **the refunds service at Acme Payments**: it is the closest to what Polderbyte's graduates build.

- It is Go on payments, the team's own stack.
- Idempotent requests and tests that prove the money adds up answer the posting's "build and run" line.
- You own the service end to end, which suits a programme that gives ownership from week one.

Then the route-planning API at Globex Logistics, for the p95 latency work: it shows you measure before you change things.

drafts.answer: I want to build payment systems that people can rely on, and Polderbyte's rails sit exactly there. At Acme Payments I am building a refunds service in Go, and the part I enjoy most is the care it takes: idempotent requests, clear states and tests that prove the money adds up. Your graduate programme would let me keep doing that work at a larger scale, with a mentor and real ownership from the first weeks. I also like that routing, refunds and settlement live in one team, so I could follow a payment from the shop to the payout. Amsterdam and an English-speaking team make it a place I can start contributing to straight away.

At Globex Logistics I worked on the route-planning API, whose slowest requests took about 900 ms at the 95th percentile. I profiled the endpoint, found that most of the time went into repeated database queries for each stop, and replaced them with one batched query and a small cache for reference data. I added a latency test to CI so the gain would not slip back. The p95 came down to 210 ms, and the planners using the tool noticed the difference the same week.

Dear Rivoli Ledger team,

I am applying for the Junior Software Engineer role on the Payments Platform. I am in the final year of a BSc in Computer Science and work part time as a backend intern at Acme Payments, where I am building a refunds service in Go. Getting every state transition right, and proving it with tests, is the part of the job I care about most, and it is what your platform asks for.

Before that, at Globex Logistics, I brought the p95 latency of a route-planning API down from 900 ms to 210 ms by batching queries and adding a latency check to CI. I work in Python and Go every day, on PostgreSQL and Docker.

My French is at B1 and I am working on it, so I could follow the finance team's discussions and grow into them.

Thank you for your time; I would be glad to talk.

[Your name]
